name: Xiaochou jing shi wo ziji (小丑竟是我自己)
blurb: "Turns out the clown was me": self-mockery after misreading a situation
title: 小丑竟是我自己 Meme: Meaning, Origin & Use
description: 小丑竟是我自己 ("turns out the clown was me") is Chinese self-mockery. It began in gaming chat in July 2020 and went viral on Baidu Tieba that December.
h1: What does 小丑竟是我自己 mean?
answer: 小丑竟是我自己 (xiǎochǒu jìng shì wǒ zìjǐ, "turns out the clown was me") is a Chinese self-mocking line for the moment you realise you were the fool: you tried hard, hoped, or felt clever, and it all backfired. It grew out of gaming streams in July 2020, where viewers called people the "clown" after a League of Legends character, and broke out in early December 2020 on the Baidu Tieba forum 抗压背锅吧, peaking around the 2021 New Year.

body: A clown entertains others and is laughed at. In the meme, the speaker discovers that the clown in the story is themselves: the person who wrote a long love message and got "ok", the worker who stayed late every night and was laid off anyway, the friend who defended someone who was lying.
Media commentators described it as self-mockery that defuses disappointment with humour. It came from the mocking form 小丑竟在我身边 ("the clown is right next to me"), turned around onto yourself.

head: Date
Event
rows: In gaming circles, the League of Legends clown champion Shaco (nicknamed 沙口) is used in stream chat to mock players: "like a Shaco, how pitiful"
In early December, users of Baidu Tieba's 抗压背锅吧 switch to the clearer "the clown is right next to me", which becomes "turns out the clown was me"
A viral Tieba story post, later admitted by its author to be made up, pushes the line far beyond the forum
Spreads to Douyin, Bilibili and WeChat sticker packs; one of the hottest memes of the New Year period

ul: Romance: "Spent a week planning a surprise and they forgot our date. 小丑竟是我自己."
Work: "Did overtime all year, got laid off in December. 小丑竟是我自己."
Shopping: "Waited for the sale, it's cheaper now than the 'discount' price I paid."
The clown emoji 🤡 used as shorthand for the same feeling
Mocking others with 小丑竟在我身边 (the clown is next to me)

body: The peak was the 2020–2021 winter. The line is now an established piece of Chinese internet vocabulary, and calling yourself or someone a 小丑 (clown) for foolish, self-defeating effort is common in everyday chat. It is closely tied to the idea of the 舔狗, someone who chases a person who does not care.

faq.q: Where does 小丑竟是我自己 come from?
faq.a: From League of Legends stream chat in mid-2020, where the clown champion was used to mock players, and then from Baidu Tieba's 抗压背锅吧 in December 2020.
No reliable source links it to the Joker. The clown in the meme is a general symbol of someone who gets laughed at.

faq.q: What does the 🤡 emoji mean in Chinese chat?
faq.a: Often the same as this meme: "I made a fool of myself" or "you are being a clown".
